title: Connecting Human Behavior and Social Robotics at ETH Zurich
summary: An ETH Zurich exchange connected Park's work on aging and robot interaction with perspectives from neuroscience and behavior.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post

paragraphs.text: How people respond to robots is a question for more than robotics alone. During a June visit to ETH Zurich, Chorong Park discussed her research with Emily S. Cross, Amol Deshmukh, and colleagues working across social robotics and human behavior.

Park presented work on human-centered AI and robotics for aging, focusing on trust, autonomy, and everyday experience. In her August 20, 2026, reflection, she highlighted the chance to hear related questions approached from different disciplines.

The exchange connected neuroscience and behavior with the design of interactive systems. For Park, that overlap offered a way to think about both what a robot does and how a person experiences the encounter.

She thanked the ETH Zurich team for hosting and welcomed opportunities to stay connected. The visit added new perspectives to an ongoing research question: how to make intelligent technologies supportive without losing sight of human choice.
